content_redacted_at.description: When the trace's content was purged. Non-null means the steps object has been deleted from storage and the content columns cleared, while this row survives as an auditable skeleton (ids, timestamps, step count). A purged trace still reads back as a skeleton with this marker set rather than as a 404, so the erasure is provable.

content_redacted_by_principal_type.description: Principal kind that purged the content ('user' or 'api_key')

content_redacted_by_principal_id.description: Public ID of the principal that purged the content — the API key's own id for key auth, so the record names which key acted.

children.description: Child traces triggered by sub-agent calls from this trace

target_id.description: Public ID of the target resource (orchestration, agent, tool, or eval)

action.description: Tool targets only — the action for mcp tools

input.description: Static input, shallow-merged under fire-time input. For `eval` targets the effective input may carry `agent_version` and `baseline_run_id`, which are passed to the queued run.

cron.description: 5-field cron expression (UTC). Present only for schedule triggers

event_pattern.description: Internal-event subscription pattern. Present only for event triggers: `*`, `prefix.*`, or an exact event name

policy_id.description: Optional boundary policy that further restricts firings

next_fire_at.description: Read-only, schedule triggers only. Server-computed next fire time

secret.description: Webhook triggers only. Returned only on create and rotate

action.description: Tool targets only — the action for mcp tools

tool_context.description:
Caller context every firing forwards to the run it starts, so an agent whose tools authorize through `{{context:<key>}}` can be put on a schedule — a firing has no request to carry one. Each key is forwarded as one `X-Naturali-Context-<key>` header.

**Write-only.** It is accepted here and never returned on a read, so the record cannot be used to recover a value.

A value may be a `{{secret:sec_...}}` reference, which keeps the credential in the [secret](/docs/modules/secrets) store and leaves only its id on the trigger; it is resolved at fire time, so rotating the secret changes the next firing without touching the trigger. A reference is refused here rather than at fire time when it is not in that id form (a secret's name does not resolve) or names a secret that does not exist in this project.

cron.description: 5-field cron expression (UTC). Required when type is schedule

event_pattern.description: Internal-event subscription pattern. Required when type is event, rejected otherwise. `*` matches every event, `prefix.*` a namespace, or give an exact event name such as `documents.ingested`

tool_context.description: Replaces the stored bag; `null` clears it. Write-only and resolved at fire time — see `CreateTriggerRequest.tool_context`.

input.description: Fire-time input, shallow-merged over the trigger's static input. For `eval` targets it may carry `agent_version` and `baseline_run_id`.

tool_context.description:
Fire-time caller context, shallow-merged per key over the trigger's stored `tool_context`. A manual fire has a caller, so this is the one path that can supply a value without storing it.

Forwarded exactly as written: a `{{secret:...}}` reference is resolved only in the trigger's stored bag, never in one supplied here.

result.description: { target_type, result_id, status, output } — output truncated

idempotency_key.description: `<event_id>:<trigger_id>` for an `event` firing, null for every other source. The same event reaching the same trigger twice produces one firing under this key, so a consumer reading firings can recognise a redelivery.

attempts.description: Dispatch attempts started. Above 1 means an earlier attempt was interrupted before it recorded a result and the firing was redelivered — not that the target refused it, which is recorded terminally in `error` and never retried.

usage_alerts.description: Email the account at 75%, 90% and 100% of its model credit, runs and indexed storage.

plan.description: The rung of the infra subscription in effect for this account: the highest it held this month. `free` for an account with no subscription, which is also the least-privileged rung. It gates the feature lines and the resource counts of the pricing table.

next_plan.description: The rung the account moves to when the month turns. It differs from `plan` only while a downgrade is pending: a downgrade takes effect at the end of the month, an upgrade at once.

retention_days.description: The longest window a project of this account may keep trace and generation content for, in days. A `PATCH` asking for a wider one — `null` included, which keeps content indefinitely — is refused with `403 plan_limit_reached`; anything shorter is always allowed. On a plan whose window a contract sets, this is that contract's figure, and `null` means nothing bounds it. A plan change that shortens the window applies at the end of the billing cycle, so this reads as the widest window held during the current one.

credit_balance_usd.description: Model credit left, in US dollars — granted and purchased credit plus the plan's monthly allowance, less managed-model and embedding spend. Managed generations and writes that embed are refused while this is negative; zero is not. Only as current as `spend_reconciled_at`, so read the two together.

earned_balance_usd.description: Marketplace earnings: the publisher's share of fees its consumers funded, less withdrawals. Never lapses.

paid_balance_usd.description: What may fund a marketplace fee: purchased credit plus earnings, less the usage included and granted credit did not cover and the fees paid. Included and granted credit never fund a fee, so a call to a priced installed tool or agent is refused with `402 insufficient_credit` while this is not positive.

spend_reconciled_at.description: When spend was last read off the meter and written to the ledger. `null` when it has never been read for at least one of the account's projects, or the account has none — a balance whose spend has never been read is not current as of anything.

storage_gb.description:
Indexed storage the account is holding, in the metered gigabytes the ceiling is enforced in — the raw file plus every chunk's text and its embedding vector, so not the size of what you uploaded.

**The account's total, not a project's.** The ceiling is pooled across every project the account pays for, so one project may hold all of it. Per project, read the `gb_day` component of `GET /v1/projects/{project_id}/usage`.

storage_limit_gb.description: The pool the account's plan allows. An ingest past it is refused with `403 plan_limit_reached` and `resource: "storage"`, whose `details` carry this figure as `limit` and what you are holding as `storage_gb`. Null where a contract sets the ceiling, or where the plan sets none.

storage_sampled_at.description:
When the **oldest** of the samples behind `storage_gb` was taken — the total is only as current as its stalest part. Measured every few minutes per project rather than on this request, so read the two together, exactly as with the balance and `spend_reconciled_at`.

Null when a project the account pays for has never been sampled, or it has no projects: a total missing a component is not current as of anything. The figure itself still reports what the samples that do exist add up to.

cycle_from.description: Start of the billing cycle the runs were counted over — the first instant of the current UTC calendar month.

runs.description: Runs this cycle across every project the account pays for. `null` when at least one project's meter could not be read: a total missing a project would understate it, and an understated count read against an allowance claims headroom that may not exist. The per-project breakdown names which one.

runs_included.description: Runs the account's plan includes per cycle. `null` on a contract plan, where the figure is commercial rather than published. Exceeding it is refused on `free` and billed as overage on `pro` and `business`.

projects.description: Every project the account pays for, oldest first, archived ones included. Empty for an account with no projects.

name.description: The project's name; `null` when it could not be read.

runs.description: Runs this cycle; `null` when this project's meter could not be read.

triggers.description: Triggers the project holds; `null` when they could not be counted.

active_channels.description: Channels in the `active` state. A `disabled` one does not count.

storage_gb.description: Indexed storage as of the last sample; `null` when the project has never been sampled.

UsageLimits.description: Each plan-capped resource, counted across every project the account pays for, beside the rung's ceiling.

used.description: How much is held; `null` when a project's part of it could not be read.

limit.description: The rung's ceiling; `null` when it sets none.

kind.description: Where the credit came from. `included` is a plan's monthly allowance and does not carry past the cycle; `purchased` is a top-up and never expires; `granted` is credit naturali gave. `usage` is managed model spend, debited from the meter. `fee` is what this account paid marketplace publishers; `earned` is its share of the fees its own listings were paid.

amount_usd.description: US dollars, signed. Negative lines are spend or corrections.

project_id.description: This account's project the line belongs to: the one whose meter produced a `usage` line, that paid a `fee` or earned an `earned`. Null for a line to the account itself.

credit_balance_usd.description: The sum of the whole ledger, not only of this page. Spend is included as it is reconciled, so read it with `spend_reconciled_at`.

spend_reconciled_at.description: When this account's managed spend was last compared against the meter — the oldest such moment across its projects. Null when at least one project has never been reconciled.

next_cursor.description: Pass as `cursor` for the next page; null on the last one.

kind.description: What was stopped: a schedule trigger is disabled, an eval run cancelled, an orchestration run or a workflow task's automation paused.

resource_id.description: The stopped trigger, eval run, orchestration run or task.

reason.description: The ceiling that stopped it: a credit balance below zero, a Free plan's runs for the month used up, or marketplace fees beyond purchased credit (`paid_balance_usd` below zero).

restorable.description: False for a cancelled eval run, which can only be dismissed.

blocked_by.description: The ceiling still closed, which blocks every restore; null when none is.

kind.description: `subscription`, `run_overage` and `prepaid` make up `total_usd` and are charged; `prepaid` is fee already paid by card at an upgrade, netted as a negative amount. The other four report movements of prepaid credit in the cycle and are not part of it.

quantity.description: For `subscription`, the share of the month the plan was held; for `run_overage`, the runs past the allowance; for `prepaid`, 1.

runs.description: Runs that month across every project the account pays for.

runs_included.description: The allowance overage was measured against.

total_usd.description: What is owed, after anything prepaid.

payment_status.description: Collection on the saved card. `unpaid` until a charge starts — within an hour of the statement, once a card is saved. `failed` moves the account to Free when the month ends.

amount_usd.description: US dollars to buy, in whole cents.

saved_card.description: Charge the saved card now instead of opening a checkout.

id.description: The payment's or the checkout's ID at the payment provider.

amount_usd.description: What is credited once paid: charged in US dollars, or its equivalent in reais.

status.description: `paid`: the saved card was charged and the credit added. `checkout`: nothing is charged until the caller pays at `checkout_url`.

checkout_url.description: The hosted page that takes the card; `null` when paid.

expires_at.description: When an unpaid checkout lapses; `null` when paid.

currency.description: What the card is charged in, from its issuing country.

exchange_rate.description: Units of `currency` per US dollar for a charge made now: 1 for `usd`, the Banco Central's latest closing PTAX selling rate for `brl`. `null` while that rate cannot be read.

id.description: The setup page's ID at the payment provider.

checkout_url.description: The hosted page that takes the card.

amount_usd.description: What each recharge buys. `null` while off.

below_usd.description: The balance under which a recharge is charged. `null` while off.

last_attempted_at.description: When a recharge was last charged, whatever its outcome.

amount_usd.description: US dollars per recharge, in whole cents.

below_usd.description: Recharge when the balance falls below this, in whole cents.

charge_usd.description: What `PUT /v1/users/me/plan` would charge now, before any conversion to reais; 0 when nothing.

charged_usd.description: What the saved card was charged now; 0 when nothing was.

checkout_url.description: The hosted page the upgrade waits on, which charges it and saves the card; `null` when nothing waits.

EventType.description: A naturali event type. The set below is what this API emits — deliberately only the events it can itself cause, so no declared name is one that never fires. It grows as modules land.

EventSubscription.description: Which events this endpoint receives. Each entry is an exact type (`generation.completed`), a resource wildcard (`generation.*`), or `*` for everything. A bare resource name (`generation`) matches nothing and is rejected.

Event.description: The envelope POSTed to your endpoint. It is also what a delivery's `payload` holds, byte for byte, so the signed body and the recorded one are the same document.

id.description: Unique per event (`evt_` prefix), and stable across redeliveries — dedupe on this if your receiver must process an event exactly once.

resource_id.description: The id of that resource, in the form its own API uses.

data.description: The resource, shaped exactly as its own API returns it — a `generation.completed` payload carries the same object `getGeneration` would.

secret.description: The signing key (`whsec_` prefix), returned only by create and rotate. Never readable afterwards.

url.description: An `https://` endpoint (`http://` is accepted for localhost, so a tunnel works in development).

WebhookUpdate.description: At least one field is required.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when there are no more.

WebhookDelivery.description: One event addressed to one endpoint, and everything that happened to it.

id.description: Public delivery ID (whd_ prefix). Sent with the request as `X-Naturali-Delivery`.

event_id.description: The event's id; shared by every delivery and redelivery of it.

status.description: `pending` until a 2xx is received (`success`) or the attempts are exhausted (`failed`). A failed delivery can be replayed with `…:redeliver`.

status_code.description: The receiver's HTTP status on the last attempt; null when the attempt never got a response (DNS, TLS, refused, timed out).

next_attempt_at.description: When the next retry is due; null once the delivery is terminal.

response_body.description: A truncated snippet of the receiver's response, or the transport error when there was no response.

next_cursor.description: Cursor for the next page, or null when there are no more.

WorkflowState.description: A named state. Exactly one state must be `initial: true`; any number may be `terminal: true`. A `kind: human` state never dispatches — the task parks until a transition fires. `on_enter` (§5) dispatches exactly one of an agent generation (`kind: agent`, `agent_id`), an orchestration run (`kind: orchestration`, `orchestration_id`) or a tool call (`kind: tool`, `tool_id`, optional `operation_id`) on entry, optionally under a `retry` policy (`max_attempts` 1-10, `backoff_seconds`, `backoff_multiplier`) that re-runs execution failures before `on_failure` applies. A `tool` dispatch settles within the dispatch and is adjudicated by the same guardrails as an orchestration `tool` node; for anything that must wait (a delay, a poll, a multi-step pipeline, or an approval-gated tool), dispatch an orchestration instead.

kind.description: `human` marks a human-in-the-loop parking state: the state never dispatches (declaring `on_enter` on it is rejected at validation) and the task parks until a principal fires a transition.

stalled_after.description: Seconds a task may sit in this state before the stall sweeper emits a `tasks.stalled` event (once per stall episode, re-armed on the next transition). Must be a positive integer when set. Omit or null to never stall. The event does not move the task — route on it with a webhook/trigger.

on_enter.description: What entering the state dispatches, and how the result routes. Omitted or null on a state that only parks.

dispatch.description: The one thing entering the state runs. `kind` picks it and names the id it needs: `agent` → `agent_id`, `orchestration` → `orchestration_id`, `tool` → `tool_id` (with an optional `operation_id`).

agent_id.description: The agent a `kind: agent` dispatch generates with.

orchestration_id.description: The orchestration a `kind: orchestration` dispatch starts a run of.

tool_id.description: The tool a `kind: tool` dispatch calls.

operation_id.description: Which operation of a multi-operation tool to invoke — the same selector an orchestration `tool` node takes.

input_mapping.description: JSON Logic building the dispatch input from the task. Carried verbatim.

payload_writes.description: JSON Logic expressions over `{task, result}` whose values are written into `task.payload` when the dispatch completes, one named channel per key. Carried verbatim.

retry.description: Re-runs the dispatch's execution failures before `on_failure` applies. Omitted means a single attempt.

backoff_multiplier.description: Factor the delay grows by per further attempt: `backoff_seconds * backoff_multiplier^(n - 2)`.

on_complete.description: Rules evaluated in order when the dispatch completes; the first whose `when` is truthy fires its transition.

when.description: JSON Logic over `{task, result}`. Carried verbatim.

transition.description: The transition to fire, by name.

on_failure.description: Transition fired when the dispatch fails after its last attempt. Omitted parks the task with `automation_status: failed`.

WorkflowTransition.description: A named, directional move. `from` is a list of source states; `to` is one target state. `guard` is a JSON Logic expression over `{task, transition, principal}` that must be truthy for the move to apply.

requires_approval.description: Gate the transition behind a human approval. When `true`, firing the transition (by anyone other than the approval resolution itself) parks a pending `ApprovalItem` instead of moving the task; the task exposes `pending_transition` until the item resolves. Approval fires the transition as the `approval` principal (its guard re-evaluated at resolution time); rejection or expiry clears the gate and appends a history note.

version.description: Incremented on every write that changes the state machine; prior versions are archived. A task pins the version it entered on, so these fields are a draft for tasks created from now on rather than a live rewrite of the ones already in flight.

version_label.description: Optional tag for the version this create archives, e.g. `initial`.
Optional tag for the version this write archives, e.g. `pre-rewire`. Ignored when the write changes no definition field, since no version is archived.

expected_version.description: Refuses the write unless the resource is at this version.

WorkflowVersion.description: An immutable archive of a workflow's state machine at one version.

id.description: Public ID of the archived version

workflow_id.description: Public ID of the workflow this version belongs to

config.description:
The workflow's versioned surface as it stood at this version: `states`, `transitions` and `payload_schema`. Name and description are metadata — bumping the version when one of them changes would make two version numbers denote the same state machine, which is exactly what a task cites.

Deliberately open rather than a fixed schema: an archive written by an earlier release of the runtime reflects the workflow surface **of its own time**, so it may carry fields the current API no longer documents.

label.description: Optional human tag for this version, e.g. `pre-rewire`. Set from the `version_label` field of a write, the `label` field of a restore, or generated for one.

created_by.description: Public ID of the user whose action produced this version. Null for writes with no request user behind them.

label.description: Optional tag for the new version the restore archives. Defaults to `restored from vN`.

Limit.name: limit
Limit.description: Results per page, 1 to 100 (default 50). Above 100 it is clamped; below 1 or not an integer it is `400`.

TagsQuery.name: tags
TagsQuery.description: Filter by tag pairs, written `key:value` (split on the first colon, so a value may contain colons). Repeat the parameter for several pairs; **all** must be present with exactly that value.

Offset.name: offset
Offset.description: Results to skip. Negative or not an integer it is `400`.

Cursor.name: cursor
Cursor.description: Opaque pagination cursor from a previous response's next_cursor.

Identifier.name: identifier
Identifier.description: The prefixed, self-describing channel identifier (`whatsapp:dm:<phone>`, `discord:dm:<user_id>`, `discord:thread:<guild_id>:<channel_id>`), URL-encoded.

GenerationId.name: generation_id
GenerationId.description: Public ID of the generation paused at `requires_action`

IfMatchVersion.name: If-Match
IfMatchVersion.description: The version the caller believes the resource holds, as an entity tag (`3` or `"3"`). Equivalent to `expected_version` in the request body; `*` states no precondition beyond the resource existing. A mismatch is `409 VERSION_CONFLICT`.

LinkToken.name: token
LinkToken.description: The single-use token from the link the Assistant sent on the channel.

MetadataQuery.name: metadata
MetadataQuery.description: A `MetadataFilter` as JSON, url-encoded. It travels as JSON rather than as `key:value` pairs because the match is exact and a query string cannot otherwise say whether `3` is the number or the string.

ModelName.name: model
ModelName.description: The model's name, as `GET /v1/models` returns it.

UsageMeterType.name: meter_type
UsageMeterType.description: Narrow the rollup to one meter type (llm_tokens, compute_execution, api_request, storage, tool_execution). Omit to include every meter. Useful with group_by=model, whose dimension otherwise mixes model ids with platform SKUs. An unrecognized value yields an empty rollup, not an error.

UsageSessionId.name: session_id
UsageSessionId.description: Narrow the whole rollup — every bucket and the top-level totals alike — to one session's traffic. Combines with group_by: group_by=day&session_id=... is one conversation's spend per day, group_by=model the same spend split by model. This is the figure behind the usage roll-up a single session read carries, broken down. An id naming no session in this project yields an empty rollup, never the project total.

UsageActorId.name: actor_id
UsageActorId.description: The same narrowing, for one end user across every session they appear in — what a customer re-billing their own users charges each of them for. An id naming no actor in this project yields an empty rollup, never the project total.

UsageAgentId.name: agent_id
UsageAgentId.description: Narrow to one agent's traffic, across every session, run and trigger that dispatched it.

UsageAiProviderId.name: ai_provider_id
UsageAiProviderId.description: Narrow to the spend billed against one provider record — a routed generation's serving target, or the agent's pinned provider.

UsageOrchestrationRunId.name: orchestration_run_id
UsageOrchestrationRunId.description: Narrow to the events one orchestration run metered.

UsageOrchestrationId.name: orchestration_id
UsageOrchestrationId.description: Narrow to the runs of one orchestration — the ones it started itself, never the subtree a loop or sub-orchestration node started under it, which is metered against the child orchestration where it was incurred. Additive: summed across a project's orchestrations the figures reach the project total exactly once.

UsageGenerationId.name: generation_id
UsageGenerationId.description: Narrow to one generation's events. A generation writes more than one when it meters several dimensions, such as tokens and compute.

UsageTraceId.name: trace_id
UsageTraceId.description: Narrow to the events recorded under one trace.

UsageSource.name: source
UsageSource.description: Narrow by what the spend was incurred for — eval and eval_judge are verification spend. Ordinary traffic carries no source, so it cannot be selected by this filter; omit the filter for everything.

UsageTriggerId.name: trigger_id
UsageTriggerId.description: Narrow to the spend one trigger initiated. Matched as recorded rather than resolved, so it still selects the spend of a trigger that has since been deleted.

UsageActionId.name: action_id
UsageActionId.description: Narrow to one caller-supplied action label, for per-action spend. Matched as recorded, like trigger_id.

Force.name: force
Force.description: When true, delete the resource together with its dependents instead of returning 409. Destructive and irreversible.

bearerAuth.description: A naturali API key (nat_sk_…) or a session JWT.

oauth2.description: A connected app's OAuth access token, issued by this API's authorization server (discovery: /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server). Its one scope carries every operation, confined to the projects the user chose when approving the app.

scopes.mcp:access: Every operation this API serves, on the projects the grant covers.

BadRequest.description: The request was malformed or failed validation.

Forbidden.description: The credential is scoped to a different project, or the caller's role in the project does not carry this action.

NotFound.description: The resource does not exist (existence is not leaked).

VersionConflict.description: The resource has moved past the version this write read (`VERSION_CONFLICT`): a stated `expected_version` or `If-Match` no longer matches, or a concurrent write took the version first. `meta.current_version` names the version in force. Nothing is written.

ApiKeyForbidden.description: Authenticated, but not permitted to act on this key.

ConversationForbidden.description: The credential cannot hold the account's conversation (`access_denied`): it is confined to one project, or it is the Assistant's own turn credential.

TurnUnavailable.description: The turn could not be run or read (`upstream_unavailable`).

AssistantUnavailable.description: This deployment serves no Assistant conversation (`assistant_unavailable`).

Conflict.description: The request conflicts with the resource's current state.

NotImplemented.description: The requested path is not enabled on this deployment (e.g. embedded signup before Meta App credentials are configured, or a Discord channel before `CHANNEL_TOKEN_KEY` is set).

UpstreamUnavailable.description: The upstream runtime, or Meta, could not complete the operation.

InstallConflict.description: `listing_suspended` (the listing cannot be installed while suspended) or `install_in_use` (resources still name the installed resource; `details.references` lists them).

ListingConflict.description: `listing_exists` (the resource already has a listing) or `invalid_listing_state` (the move is not allowed from the listing's current state).

ListingModelNotPriced.description: `model_not_priced`: the agent runs on a naturali model that has no price yet, so its use could not be billed.

StopNotFound.description: No such stop on this account, or it was already restored or dismissed.

StopNotRestorable.description: The stop cannot be restored now.

StopRestoreUnavailable.description: The runtime could not turn the item back on; the stop stays listed.

WebhookLimitReached.description: The project already holds 20 webhooks (`webhook_limit_reached`); `details.limit` carries the ceiling.

SealingKeyNotConfigured.description: The requested path is not enabled on this deployment — a webhook secret cannot be stored where no credential-sealing key is configured.
